rules.reason: The page title establishes the primary reading level.
Task pages reserve room for data and controls.
A section groups related content rather than promoting each child.
Section titles remain subordinate to a task, commerce or reading page title.
Nested surfaces use the existing smaller inset relation S05.
A feature card explains one concept; its title and copy form one group.
Product identity and price take precedence over a promotional heading.
Author and metadata identify reading content; preserve its editorial hierarchy.
Supporting information does not compete with task page headings.
Give values and mixed-script glyphs sufficient room before reducing their font; decoration is secondary.
Fields form a group; label/help proximity stays smaller than field separation.
Settings use the same field grammar as forms, within a task context.
Repeated data rows follow density rather than a fixed cell padding.
List items remain related within their enclosing component.
Hero copy is one group; the action is the next group. Media fits its content box instead of viewport-based negative bleed.
Two columns require room in the containing region, independently of viewport width.
The existing orphan-free flow owns column selection; content supplies its minimum cell width.
A primary form uses the existing larger inset; a secondary form retains the component inset.
Main and supporting content must fit their allocated region before taking two columns.
Names, roles and biographies determine the reading capacity of each person cell.
Plan columns reuse orphan-free flow with room for the price and feature list.
A primary offer groups its identity, price, features and action.
An offer in a supporting region uses the smaller existing surface inset.
A testimonial fits its own box; attribution remains attached to the quotation.
A reading-page citation retains the existing editorial treatment.
Chart and legend share the available box while full values remain in the data table.
The existing calendar container switches to its full-text agenda when cells cannot fit events.
Media columns and thumbnail placement depend on the gallery region, not the viewport.
Release metadata and descriptions use separate tracks with bounded reading measures.
Label and value keep proximity and stack when inline labels would consume the region.
Menu text and prices retain separate roles inside a content-sized cell.
Selection and detail tracks stack inside a narrow allocated region.
Copy and action share one group and wrap in their own container.
Feature descriptions supply the minimum readable flow cell.
Repeated steps reuse the same content-sized flow as other repeated information.
